items.title: Chuck Findley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 6, 2023
items.q: I had a teacher by the name of Harry Herforth in Cleveland when I was in high school.

ctx.x: No I was thinking of almost like a childrens’ book and an aspiration to be a musician and how these wonderful things kept happening to you but that you were ready.

Well you know the training I had, like I said before, the training is very, very important. I mean you know Uan Rasey used to — okay let me give you this. I had a teacher by the name of Harry Herforth in Cleveland when I was in high school. Now before him the first teacher was a vaudeville trumpet player in Cleveland. And I did some — I even did a vaudeville gig. And it was one that was real vaudeville, it was down in Short Vincent in Cleveland and with an actual, you know, it was a burlesque show with the girls,…

watch the show and play to the show. And mainly added [sings] Ta-da you know when, ‘cause they had great comedians too. There was one comedian, oh I can’t think of his name at all but he was kind of a famous vaudeville comedian anyhow. And one of his — they did a line, a bit where he said to one of the girls he says, “What is your favorite song?” And she says, “The ‘William Tell Overture.’” And I can’t really tell this ‘cause the kids’ll see it but it was a rump-titty-rump-rump-rump. Right? Well you can imagine…
